author: Audrey Mayer
title: Nashville high rise apartments strike deal to get private Music City Loop station - NewsBreak
text:
By Audrey Mayer ,
4 hours ago
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WKRN) — Three downtown Nashville apartment buildings are set to have private access to the Music City Loop through a residential station.
The apartments are along Church Street including Prime, Alcove, and the soon-to-be-tallest building in Tennessee, Paramount.
The deal between Elon Musk’s The Boring Company and long-time Nashville real estate developer Tony Giarratana marks The Boring Company’s first residential agreement for the Music City Loop project.
⏩ Read today’s top stories on wkrn.com
“Just getting around downtown can get a little hectic, so if I can catch a flight easily, nine minutes from here if I’m running late. I really love that being a resident here,” Nashville resident Salma Selleaze told News 2.
The Boring Company said the project will allow residents to take an elevator within their building directly to a Loop station, board a Tesla and be at the airport in about nine minutes and Lower Broadway in about two minutes.
Giarratana tells News 2 he expects The Boring Company to drill underneath his buildings within two months.
“The Boring Company concept, I scratched my head about it until I experienced it in Las Vegas, and that sold me; and so when they walked in the door and said, ‘Let’s take a look at your buildings,’ we jumped all over it,” Giarratana explained.
Giarratana said the residential station will serve about 1,000 residents living in Prime and Alcove, and in 2028, about 750 more residents living in Paramount.

“All of the 706 units [in Prime and Alcove] access these elevators each day. And so The Boring Company, because that drill is below grade, it will be about 30 feet down. It will connect at the lowest level of this garage on what we call B3,” Giarratana said.
The Music City Loop project has faced resistance from local leaders. In March , the Metro Council voted to formally oppose the project citing concerns over transparency, community engagement and safety. However, Giarratana said he sees the Music City Loop project as an opportunity for Nashville.
“I personally think that Nashville’s going to wake up one day instead of feeling, ‘Gosh, we failed. We didn’t do a light rail system when we had the chance,’ but now, with autonomous vehicles and this tunnel system, we’re going to wake up and look like we’re geniuses that we didn’t do those things, that we’re taking part of the new technology of the future. I think it’s going to be a win-win,” Giarratana said.
